newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Woodside says repairs Cossack platform.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Woodside says repairs Cossack platform.

text.p: Woodside Petroleum Ltd said on Tuesday it has repaired a faulty system at its Cossack-Pioneer oil platform off the coast of Western Australia.
A Woodside spokesman said that lost production would gradually be restored as a result of the repair work, although he could not say at what rate the platform was currently producing crude.
"You don't just turn production back on, you gradually build it up," he said.
The Cossack-Pioneer's output fell to about 50,000 barrels a day in October versus a design capacity of 115,000 barrels due to difficulties with the facility's gas export system.
The Cossack-Pioneer reportedly had been producing on average about 90,000 barrels a day prior to the curtailment.

The platform pumps crude oil and gas from the Wanaea and Cossack fields in the North West Shelf, has been plagued by weater-related and technical problems since it was commissioned in November last year.

Equal partners in the North West Shelf are units of Broken hill Pty Co Ltd, The British Petroleum Co Plc, Japan Australia LNG (MiMi) Pty Ltd, a partnership of Mitsui & Co Ltd and Mitsubishi Corp, Chevron Corp, Royal Dutch/Shell Group and Woodside.
